decisions.quote:
Summary
DOES READING LITERATURE RESULT IN HIGHER EMPATHY? A REPLICATION STUDY
K. DIJKSTRA, P. VERKOEIJEN, I. VAN KUIJK, S. YEE CHOW, A. BAKKER & R. ZWAAN
A recently published paper in Science (Kidd & Castano, 2013) showed in five experiments that
  reading literary fiction led to an increase in performance on tests of affective and cognitive
  Theory of Mind when compared with reading popular fiction, nonfiction or no reading.
  Although the authors only claim that this is a temporary effect, the claim itself is remarkable
  and warrants further examination. The current study is a replication study of one the exper-
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify this work as a replication. Primary evidence confirms that Dijkstra et al. (2015) collected new data from an independent sample of 528 US Mechanical Turk participants (300 after exclusions) to re-test Experiment 5 of Kidd & Castano (2013) using the same text materials and Theory of Mind tasks (RMET and Yoni).

decisions.location: Summary, p. 19, lines 471-475 (and Reference list, p. 19, lines 536-539)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify the same tested original paper: Kidd & Castano (2013), 'Reading Literary Fiction Improves Theory of Mind', Science, 342, 377-380. Specifically, the authors re-test Experiment 5 from Kidd & Castano (2013).

decisions.quote:
The results of this
  study demonstrate that the findings of this original study do not replicate in an indepen-
  dent study with a similar population and the exact same materials and tasks.
decisions.reason: With the dependent original identity resolved to Kidd & Castano (2013) and the study type established as a replication, the authors' explicit overall replication verdict governs: the findings of the original study do not replicate (neither on RMET nor on the Yoni task). Both the shipped record and blind coding correctly code the outcome as 'failed' (replacing the shipped English translation of the reflection box and the blind coder's column-joined quote with a literal contiguous passage from the paper's English Summary).
